newsitem.title: USA: Texas court remands Entergy to regulators.
newsitem.headline: Texas court remands Entergy to regulators.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Friday the Texas Supreme Court remanded to the Public Utility Commission of Texas a rate case seeking to have certain River Bend nuclear plant costs included in customer rates.
The court's action requires that the commission to again consider Entergy Gulf States' request for favorable rate treatement of the original construction costs of River Bend, the utility explained.
A May 1988 commission decision placed $1.453 billion in abeyance, with no finding as to prudence. Entergy's appeal of this decision led to Friday's court ruling.

"We are pleased by this decision of the Texas Supreme Court," Entergy said. "Sending the case back to the Public Utility Commission is the only fair and equitable course. We'll now have an opportunity to make our case before the commission, and we're confident the commission will resolve this issue fairly and equitably."

The court, in its order, said "...we conclude that the Public Utility Commission prejudiced (Entergy) Gulf States' substantial rights by attempting to defer ruling on the proper treatment of the $1.453 billion. We therefore reverse the PUC's order and remand the case to the PUC for further proceedings."

Additionally, Entergy said, the court ruled in the same case that the commission incorrectly determined the amount of federal income tax expense that Entergy Gulf States should have been allowed in rates.

The court noted the commission had used an actual-taxes-paid method. However, the court ruled in 1995 (Public Utility Commission v. GTE-Southwest, Inc.) that the commission could not consider deductions for disallowed expenses in determining a utility's federal income tax liability. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
